Multi-directional Recurrant Neural Networks : A novel Method for Estimating missing Data.
Most time-series datasets with many missing measurements that need estimation. The most existing methods address this problem either by interpolations within data streams or by imputing across them; we develop a new method that does both.
M-RNNs are a novel method for estimating missing data in time series data streams, they outperform state-of-the-art methods, and that they can be applied to real-world medical datasets.

1) M-RNNs can be applied to the task of imputing missing data in multivariate time-series data; 2) the M-RNN architecture can outperform the standard bi-directional RANN architecture in this task; 3) this architecture is especially useful in the context of multivariate time-series datasets where there are multiple data streams, and 4) this architecture can be applied in the context of medical data to improve the accuracy of imputation of missing measurements.

the problem of estimating missing data in time series.
the problem of imputation of missing values in multi-variate time series data.
